statement: guides/spin2-getting-started.yaml:208-210 teaches a one-line `IF condition THEN statement` form (syntax `IF condition THEN statement`, example `IF (x > 100) THEN x := 100`). Spin2 has no THEN keyword and no one-line IF: the body goes on the following indented lines (`grep -n -i THEN` over spin2-v55-text.txt returns English-prose hits only, no IF form with THEN). BASIC habit. Sibling of S-075 (`IF cond : stmt`, another invented one-line IF); the arbiter may merge the two into one class.

statement: language/fundamentals/pasm-labels.yaml:46-62 (`usage_examples.global_and_local.code`, the page's only complete routine) uses `jnz .loop`. PASM2 has no JNZ instruction (conditional jumps are `IF_NZ JMP #label`, or TJNZ/DJNZ on a register); the assembler stops at it. Behind that error the block has two more faults that only show once JNZ is fixed: `cmp x, #10` carries no WZ/WC, so no flag is written for the branch to test; and `tjz temp, :retry` names the local label as the S operand without `#` (a register address, not a jump target: TJZ D,{#}S needs `#:retry`). JNZ is another assembler family's mnemonic (P1 has no JNZ either), an invented instruction like S-080's.

statement: variable-scoping-best-practices.yaml teaches local / parameter / return names shadowing a VAR or DAT name as legal; the compiler refuses all of them as duplicate names. Four gated sites: :55 (`PUB method(value) : count | temp` over `LONG count`, m230), :96 (`PUB check_device() : status` over `LONG status`, m230), :113 (`PUB fill_buffer(buffer, size)` over DAT `buffer`, m221), :129 (`PUB process() | index` over `LONG index`, m241). Prose that teaches the same wrong rule, not gated: :21-29 (`precedence_order` 1..6 'Higher precedence shadows lower'), :50-52, :64-65 ('VAR count is inaccessible', 'VAR count is never modified'), :152-161 (debugging_shadowing symptoms). The page's own fixed_code and best-practice rules (distinct names) are correct and compile; only the premise that the shadowing compiles is wrong.
